messages:
Alex Kim: Hi everyone, starting my first day! Quick question about Slack norms — where should I post onboarding/setup questions vs product bug reports? Also when is it better to DM someone vs post in a channel? :wave:
Lauren P: welcome Alex! :tada: For setup/onboarding Qs, post in #new-hires or DM People Ops depending on privacy. For infra or creds issues use #help-it. Bug reports -> open in #support or #product-bugs so engineers can triage. DM if it's personal data or account details.
Maria G: +1. For engineering questions about code or infra, post in the team channel (e.g., #eng-runtime) and always thread replies so we don't spam the main feed. If it's a quick yes/no, DM is fine.
Samir: also note: use @here sparingly. If something is urgent for the oncall, ping @oncall in #incidents — that's the escalation path. For access requests, mention IT Helpdesk or file through the portal.
IT Helpdesk: Hi Alex — welcome! If you need access, run the onboarding bot in DMs: `@it-helpdesk start-onboarding` or visit https://intranet.redwood/it-onboarding. We can invite you to channels if you list which ones.
Lauren P: one more tip — intro posts go in #new-hires or #random with a short blurb + :wave:. Keep intros ~1–3 sentences (team, what you’ll be working on, fun fact). People love a quick hook.
Ops Bot: FYI: automated deploy and incident pings post in #release-war-room and #incidents respectively. Reactions are fine to ack messages; threads for follow-ups.
Alex Kim: thanks! quick follow-up — I tried to join #eng-runtime but it says private. Should I request invite here or DM Samir?
Samir: just post the channel name here and I’ll /invite you. Or use `/invite @alex.kim #eng-runtime`. If you hit permissions, ping me directly.
Alex Kim: perfect, thanks all! Adding #eng-runtime to the list I need access to. Appreciate the quick orientation. :smile:
